help.title: Help
team.stats.title: Team stats
team.stats.legend: V = win · E = draw · D = loss
team.stats.help:
Matches counted: the team's fixtures that are finished or already played with a score recorded (match report or fixture score). Future matches are not counted.

V/E/D: wins, draws and losses in those matches.

Win rate: points ÷ (matches × 3), with a win worth 3 points, a draw 1 and a loss 0.

Cards, top scorer and top points come from the match report and the team's athletes' performance in the last 40 fixtures.

Recent fixtures: the latest matches that count, with the result from this team's point of view.
mural.rule.title: How it was calculated
peladas.help:
This screen has four entries: Kickabouts, Matches, Teams and People.

Each list has its own search and shows the same neighbourhood first, then the same city and the same county.

Tap an item to open the detail. In Kickabouts, + creates a new one.
confrontos.help:
Tap a fixture (or Join) to see details, score and sign-ups. Use Schedule new fixture/match to challenge an opponent.

Fixtures near your area appear first. When scheduling, enter the date, time and venue; both teams' diaries are checked before sending and before accepting.

Full details: see the app manual.
mural.app.help:
General: ratings and goals from fixtures count 3× only for ordering the rankings; the cards show the real values. Tie: the oldest participant.

Teams and coaches: win 3 pts, draw 1 pt, defeat 0 pts.

Full details: see the app manual.
mural.confrontos.help:
Best team in the app: the team that has played the most fixtures wins; on a tie, the best win rate wins (win 3 pts, draw 1 pt, defeat 0 pts).

Longest unbeaten run: counting starts at the most recent fixture and goes back in time until the first defeat. We show the unbeaten days and the starting date.

Best attack and best defence: taken from the fixtures' match report score — goals for and goals against, with the average per match. The top scorer and the top points defender come from the performance of the team's players.

The region filter (county, city and neighbourhood) applies to all of these cards.
mural.app.bestTeam.title: Best team in the app
mural.app.longestUnbeaten.title: Longest unbeaten run
mural.app.bestAttack.title: Best attack
mural.app.bestDefense.title: Best defence
mural.app.bestPelada.title: Best pelada in the app
mural.rule.melhorTime.default: The team that has played the most fixtures wins. On a tie in fixtures played, the best win rate wins (win 3 pts, draw 1 pt, defeat 0 pts).
mural.rule.invencibilidade.default: The run is counted from the most recent fixture backwards, until the first defeat. The card shows the unbeaten days, how many fixtures are in the run and the starting date.
mural.rule.melhorAtaque.default: The team with the most goals scored in fixtures wins, according to the match report score. The card also shows the goals per match and the team's top scorer.
mural.rule.melhorDefesa.default: The team with the fewest goals conceded in fixtures wins, according to the match report score. The card also shows the average per match and the team's top points defender.
mural.rule.melhorPelada.default: A pelada counts only with at least one held event in this filter: finished, or the end time has already passed. A fixture does not count. Order: most held events; then the higher average of filled mural cards, of different profiles, of participants per event, of distinct voters and of votes; then fewer red cards and fewer yellow cards; last, cash movement, a confirmed cotinha and a pelada message. A full tie goes to the pelada registered earliest in the app.
mural.rule.topPeladas.default: The first 10 peladas, in the same order as Best pelada in the app: most held events; then higher averages of filled mural cards, profiles, participants per event, voters and votes; then fewer red cards and fewer yellow cards; last, cash, cotinha and messages. A full tie goes to the pelada registered earliest in the app.
screen.help.event-mural-media-hub: Here you choose how to follow the event coverage: radio, newspaper or video. Tip: come back after the match, as the hired professionals publish commentary, reports and highlights throughout the event.
screen.help.event-mural-media-video: This screen shows the event highlights video, uploaded by the camera operator. Tip: if there is no video yet, come back later. Watch and share the best moments with the lads.
screen.help.event-mural-media-radio: Here you listen to the goal commentary and the event interview, recorded by the commentator. Tip: use headphones to enjoy it more. If nothing has been published yet, come back after the match.
screen.help.event-mural-media-journal: Here you read the event newspaper, with the report and the interview written by the journalist. Tip: switch between Report and Interview at the top. If nothing has appeared yet, come back after the match.
screen.help.event-journalist-journal: On this screen you, as the journalist, write and publish the event report and interview on the wall. Tip: add an eye-catching headline and a good photo. Scroll down and review the text before sending.
screen.help.event-narrator-radio: Here you, as the commentator, record or upload the goal commentary (up to 40 seconds) and the interview (up to 50 seconds) for the event wall. Tip: record somewhere quiet and listen back before sending. A new upload replaces the previous one.
screen.help.event-cameraman-coverage: On this screen you, as the camera operator, upload the event highlights video to the wall, up to 5 minutes long. Tip: give it a short, catchy title and description. A new video replaces the previous one.
screen.help.event-coach-board: This is the coach's board: briefing checklist, formation, tactical focus, suggested starters and substitutions for each team. Tip: tick off the checklist during the warm-up and save the board before kick-off.
screen.help.event-physical-trainer: Here you put together the fitness plan: focus, duration, notes and players present at the session. Tip: save the plan before the match and use the buttons to start and finish the warm-up. Once the event starts, the screen becomes read-only.
screen.help.event-masseur-treatments: On this screen you log quick treatments: player, moment, body area, type, duration and whether they can return to play. Tip: log each treatment straight after it. This is not a medical record, just support for the team.
screen.help.event-fan-checkin: Here you confirm you are supporting, at the ground or from afar, and leave a message for the team. Tip: check in before the match and send an upbeat message. See who else is cheering too.
screen.help.event-supplementary-hiring: On this screen you invite assistants to the event: assistant referees or scouts. Tip: search by name or nickname, check the profile before choosing and set a fair fee and deadline. Follow the reply in Sent invitations.
screen.help.athlete-profile-form: Here you update your player profile and how much you charge to take part. Tip: keep your details complete and your fees clear. That makes it easier to be invited to kickabouts and matches.
screen.help.athlete-profile-hiring: On this screen you choose a personal fitness coach and scout to follow your performance. Tip: search by name, check the profile before choosing and save your preferences at the end.
screen.help.athlete-profile-view: This is the player's profile: location, kickabouts, teams, goals, wins, cards, idols and performance logged by the scout. Tip: switch between Profile and Performance to see the numbers from each match. Play more to improve your stats.
screen.help.fan-profile-form: Here you adjust your supporter profile and how much you charge to watch kickabouts and matches, in person or from afar. Tip: name, photo, favourite teams and idols are edited in My details. Accept the commitments to be hired.
screen.help.role-profile-form: On this screen you update your professional details for this role and see your kickabouts, matches and teams. Tip: keep your fees up to date to receive more invitations. Favourite teams and idols are edited in My details.
screen.help.profile-view: This is the person's profile in this role: location, favourite team, idols, kickabouts, matches and the numbers from their work. Tip: check their history and scores in kickabouts before inviting or hiring someone.
screen.help.legends-hub: Here are the legends of amateur football: players and teams that made history. Tip: search before adding one, so you do not duplicate an existing entry. Legends appear as suggestions on profiles.
screen.help.legend-athlete-form: On this screen you add a legendary amateur football player: photo, nickname, position, where they lived and the teams they played for. Tip: look up the address by postcode (CEP) and pick the teams from the list. If they have passed away, tick In memoriam.
screen.help.legend-athlete-view: Here you see the story of a legendary player: position, end of career, where they lived, the teams they played for and who added them. Tip: tap the teams to learn more about the history of amateur football.
screen.help.legend-team-form: On this screen you add a legendary team: image, name, dates, where it was from, its story and the players who played for it. Tip: put some care into the About the team text and add legendary or app players to the squad.
screen.help.legend-pro-athlete-form: Here you add a legendary professional player: photo, nickname, position, where they lived and the professional teams they played for. Tip: look up the address by postcode (CEP) and pick the teams from the list. If they have passed away, tick In memoriam.
screen.help.account-edit: On this screen you edit your details: name, nickname, email, mobile, address, idols, favourite team and password. Tip: keep your address correct to see events near you and appear in the rankings. Choose whether to show your mobile and email on your profile.
screen.help.about: Here you see the app version, who developed it, the website, the user manual and the Controle de Bola social media. Tip: follow us on Facebook, use Invite Friends to bring in your kickabout mates and send feedback, suggestions or problems via Contact us.
screen.help.contact-message: On this screen you send a message to the Controle de Bola team. Tip: write a clear title and describe well what happened. If it is a problem, attach a screenshot to help us fix it.
screen.help.login: Here you sign in with email or mobile and password. Tip: set up biometrics in the menu after your first sign-in. Forgotten your password? Request a 6-digit code by email (not a magic link), check spam and enter it on this screen; after sending, a card shows your masked email.
screen.help.register: On this screen you create your Controle de Bola account. Tip: choose a nickname that is easy to recognise at events and select your address from the suggestions list to see kickabouts near you. You can add your mobile later.
screen.help.onboarding: Welcome to Controle de Bola! Here you tell us how you take part in amateur football: kickabout, amateur team or other roles. Tip: choose the option that suits you best so the app starts your way.
screen.help.profile-setup: On this screen you build your football profile: player, supporter or another role, with your fees and your Pix key. Tip: fill it in now to be found in kickabouts and rankings. If you prefer, tap Complete later.
screen.help.home: This is the app Home: choose Kickabouts, Matches, Teams or Users to browse lists and details. Tap a door to enter; use the home icon in the top bar to return here. The Kickabouts tab at the bottom opens the kickabout list directly.
screen.help.peladas: Here are the kickabouts you take part in or that are near you, with the sport, venue, average turnout and organiser. Tap a kickabout or Join to see the details. Use the + button to create your own kickabout and get the lads together.
screen.help.events: Here you see fixtures between teams: accepted challenges that still need a date and scheduled matches, with the next one highlighted. Tap an accepted challenge to set the date, venue and squad call-up. Pull down to refresh the list.
screen.help.mural: The Wall shows highlights and rankings in General, Kickabouts and Fixtures. On General you will see a confidence hint on the table; on Player of the Match, when there are votes, it shows how many people rated. Switch tabs, use each card's ? and pull down to refresh.
screen.help.search: Search for events, people's profiles and amateur teams, using the type filters to find things faster. Tap a result to open the details, the team sheet or its fixtures. You can also add amateur football legends, whether players or teams.
screen.help.profile: This is your account: your details, inbox, your profiles (player, supporter and other roles), your teams and the kit manager's equipment. Complete your profiles to be found and hired. Turn on biometric sign-in to get in faster and invite your friends to the app.
screen.help.pelada-detail: This is the kickabout page: events, members, join requests, fees, pots and kitty. Tap ? on the bar for this summary and Listen to hear it aloud. If you organise, create events, approve join requests and keep accounts up to date.
screen.help.pelada-form: Here you create or edit a kickabout, with its name, venue address and photos. Fill in the full address so players in the area can find your kickabout. Adding a photo of the venue and of the admin gives more confidence to anyone who wants to join.
screen.help.event-detail: Date, venue, score, goals, referee, hires and voting (0–10; at most two 10s per person, with a counter on screen). Sign up with the action buttons. If you organise, confirmed participants show in a compact card under Participants; notify them, track arrival and goalkeepers.
screen.help.event-create: Here you create a new event, with name, type, teams, date, time, venue, participation fee and gate control. Check the date, time and venue before saving. If there is a charge, add a PIX key to make payment easier for participants.
screen.help.event-register: Here you sign up for the next match, seeing the fee, the player limit and your link to the kickabout. Keep your player profile up to date before signing up. If there is a charge, pay via PIX straight afterwards so the organiser can confirm your place.
screen.help.event-team-split: Here you split the confirmed players into the match teams, by hand or automatically. Choose a criterion, such as random, members first, neighbourhoods or favourite team, to balance the sides. In manual mode, tap a player or drag them to the team you want.
screen.help.event-predictions: Make your predictions for the match: who will score the most goals, which goalkeeper will concede the fewest and the final result. Make your predictions before the event starts. Add the scorers you believe in and tap Save predictions to take part.
screen.help.event-sumula: The match report records what happened in the game: the score and the details of each player from both teams. Search for a player by nickname to find them quickly. Write clear notes about the players and remember to save the report at the end.
screen.help.event-scout-apontamento: Here the scout logs the players' actions during the match, in Individual or General mode. In Individual mode, first choose the player you are going to follow. Log each action as it happens so the performance data is more accurate.
screen.help.inbox: Your messages are split into Inbox and Outbox: invitations, challenges, reschedules, join requests and refereeing for fixtures. Reply quickly to challenges and invitations so you do not miss the match. In the Outbox, keep track of what you have sent and are still awaiting a reply on.
inbox.help:
The Inbox keeps everything you have received; the Outbox keeps everything you have sent. Nothing is deleted once the matter is settled: the date and time are recorded so you can check back later.

At the top you find the items that still need your reply. Below that sits the full message history.

An unread message shows in bold with a highlight dot; opening it clears the highlight and lowers the number on the mail icon.

Search finds a message by any word in the subject, the text or the person's name — no need to match accents or capitals.

screen.help.team-profile: This is the team sheet, with location, average age, squad, wins, draws and defeats, win rate, cards, top scorer and latest fixtures. Read the match report notes to get to know the team's style. Use this information before challenging or accepting a match.
screen.help.team-form: Here you add or edit your team, with images, badge, clubhouse photo, kit and squad. Add the squad players so you can call them up for fixtures. Adding a badge and kit makes the team easier to recognise.
screen.help.desafio-create: Here you challenge another team, first seeing their average age, wins, cards and latest matches. Choose the team, enter the preferred date, time and venue and send the challenge. You need a registered team to send a challenge.
screen.help.confronto-create: Here you schedule the fixture for an accepted challenge, with home team, away team, first-leg date and, if you like, the return leg. Call up the players from your squad for the match. If there is no accepted challenge yet, use the Go to Challenge button.
screen.help.material-inventory: Here you manage the equipment: kits by colour and quantity, damaged items and gear. Add a row for each item and remove anything that no longer exists. Keep the quantities up to date and tap save at the end.
screen.help.event-gate-scan: This screen reads QR code tickets at the event entrance and shows whether they are valid. Tap Start scanning and point the camera at the participant's QR code. Make sure there is good light and hold the phone steady so it scans faster.
screen.help.event-gate-entries: Here you see who has already entered the event, with their role, entry time and who authorised it. Use this list to check participants' attendance. Go back to the event screen to scan new tickets.
screen.help.event-mural: The event wall brings together the press coverage, with newspaper, radio and video, the match highlights and the Top 10 for each profile. Tap newspaper, radio or video to see the content. Use the "?" on each card to understand how it was calculated.
mural.rule.craque.evento: The winner is the player with the highest sum of ratings in the event vote; the card shows that sum. Each voter counts once. With fewer than 3 voters only a notice appears.
mural.rule.goleador.evento: The winner scored the most goals in the event. Tie at the top: all are shown, in alphabetical order.
mural.rule.goleador.evento_pelada: The winner scored the most goals in the event. Goals come from the referee sheet or the scout, per the group's preference. Tie at the top: all are shown.
mural.rule.goleador.evento_confronto: The winner scored the most goals in the match. Goals come from the referee sheet first; without it, the scout counts. Tie at the top: all are shown.
mural.rule.goleiro.evento: The winner is the goalkeeper with the highest sum of ratings; the card shows the average. Ties: the oldest wins. With fewer than 3 voters only a notice appears.
mural.rule.timeAmado.evento: The favourite professional club most named among the event's players; the card shows how many fans. "No team" does not count. Ties: alphabetical order.
mural.rule.promessa.evento: The youngest player in the event, counting only those with a date of birth. Same age: alphabetical order.
mural.rule.master.evento: The oldest player in the event, counting only those with a date of birth.
mural.rule.juiz.evento: The winner is the referee with the highest sum of ratings in the event; the card shows that sum. With fewer than 3 voters only a notice appears.
mural.rule.participantesLocal.evento: No winner. Counts the event's participants by city and neighbourhood of their profile address and shows the overall total.
mural.rule.torcida.evento: Ranks fans who checked in to the event: in person is worth 12 points, remote 10. Shows up to 10.
mural.rule.desempenho.evento: Shows the top 3 for each scout stat in the event (shots, assists, passes, fouls) by each player's total. Charts add up the event's numbers.
mural.rule.palpites.evento: Scored after the event: top scorer +3, least-beaten goalkeeper +3, each player's exact goals +1, each yellow +1 and each red +2. Highest total first.
mural.rule.palpites.evento_confronto: Scored after the match: score +2 per side right and +1 if exact; top scorer +3, least-beaten goalkeeper +3, exact goals +1, yellow +1, red +2. Highest total first.
mural.rule.supportOps.evento: No ranking. Summarises event support: coach checklist (x/3), trainer warm-up, masseur treatments and alerts, and fan check-ins.
mural.rule.top10.evento: For each role, lists the 10 with the highest sum of ratings in the event; the badge shows the average. Goalkeeper ties: more votes, then the oldest. Fewer than 3 voters: notice only.
mural.rule.eventMedia.evento: No ranking. Lists what was published for the event: newspaper (report or interview), radio (commentary or interview) and highlights video.
mural.rule.top10Hub.evento: Opens Top 10 rankings by role: athletes, goalkeepers, and under Other: referees, journalists, cameramen, narrators and ball boys/girls.
mural.rule.scoutHub.evento: Summarises scout notes for the event: qualitative and quantitative tops, aggregate charts and goals by type.
mural.rule.goalTypes.evento: Event totals for each goal type recorded by the scout (header, free kick, feet, Olympic, crazy and penalty).
mural.rule.notasIndividuais.evento: Lists 0–10 ratings participants gave to the scout, masseur and kit man, highest first.
mural.rule.curiosidades.evento: Extra event stats: where participants come from, favourite teams, athlete height and fan check-ins.
mural.rule.sumulaConsulta.evento: Any logged-in user can view the match sheet. Only the confirmed referee edits within the admin time window.
mural.rule.timeAmador.evento: Most cited amateur favourite team among event registrants; shows how many athletes picked it.
mural.rule.altura.evento: Among athletes with height on profile, shows tallest and shortest (tie: alphabetical).
mural.rule.torcidaCheckins.evento: Count of fans who checked in at this event (in person or remote), not a ranking.
mural.rule.craque.geral: The winner is the player with the most points added up from ratings (match ratings count 3x for ordering only). The card shows the real average rating. Goalkeepers are excluded.
mural.rule.craque.peladas: The winner is the player with the most points added up from ratings in pickup games. The card shows the average rating. Goalkeepers are excluded.
mural.rule.craque.confrontos: The winner is the player with the most points added up from ratings in team matches. The card shows the average rating. Goalkeepers are excluded.
mural.rule.goleador.geral: The winner has the most goals; for ordering, each team-match goal counts 3. The card shows the real goal total (pickup + matches). Ties: all are shown.
mural.rule.goleador.peladas: The winner scored the most goals in pickup games. The card shows that total. Ties: all are shown.
mural.rule.goleador.confrontos: The winner scored the most goals in team matches. The card shows that total. Ties: all are shown.
mural.rule.goleiro.geral: The winner is the goalkeeper with the most rating points (match ratings count 3x for ordering only). The card shows the real average rating. Ties: the oldest wins.
mural.rule.goleiro.peladas: The winner is the goalkeeper with the most rating points in pickup games. The card shows the average rating. Ties: the oldest wins.
mural.rule.goleiro.confrontos: The winner is the goalkeeper with the most rating points in team matches. The card shows the average rating. Ties: the oldest wins.
mural.rule.timeAmado.default: The professional club chosen as favourite team by the most participants. Shows how many fans it has. Ties: alphabetical order.
mural.rule.promessa.default: The youngest player among participants who entered a date of birth. Same age: alphabetical order by name.
mural.rule.master.default: The oldest player among participants who entered a date of birth.
mural.rule.juiz.geral: The winner is the referee with the most rating points (match ratings count 3x for ordering only). The card shows the real average rating.
mural.rule.juiz.peladas: The winner is the referee with the most rating points in pickup games. The card shows the average rating.
mural.rule.juiz.confrontos: The winner is the referee with the most rating points in team matches. The card shows the average rating.
mural.rule.atletas.geral: The 10 with the most rating points make the list (match ratings count 3x to get in), ordered by real average rating. Ties: more votes, then the oldest.
mural.rule.atletas.peladas: The 10 with the most rating points in pickup games, ordered by average rating. Ties: more votes, then the oldest.
mural.rule.atletas.confrontos: The 10 with the most rating points in team matches, ordered by average rating. Ties: more votes, then the oldest.
mural.rule.times.default: Teams ranked by team-match points: win 3, draw 1. Ties: higher win rate first; teams tied in 10th place are also shown.
mural.rule.treinadores.default: Coaches ranked by team-match points: win 3, draw 1. Ties: the oldest first; coaches tied in 10th place are also shown.
mural.rule.apoio.default: For each professional, averages the ratings in each game, then averages across games. The top 10 are shown. Ties: more votes, then the oldest.
mural.rule.palpites.geral: Adds up points from correct predictions; for ordering, team-match points count 3x. The card shows the real points. Ties: more games predicted, then the oldest.
mural.rule.palpites.peladas: Adds up points from correct predictions in pickup games. Ties: more games predicted, then the oldest.
mural.rule.palpites.confrontos: Adds up points from correct predictions in team matches. Ties: more games predicted, then the oldest.
mural.rule.participantesLocal.default: Counts app participants by state, city and neighbourhood, using the profile address. Places with the most people come first.
mural.rule.desempenho.default: Adds up game stats (shots, passes, assists, fouls) and shows the top 3 for each. Charts show totals and accuracy percentages.
mural.rule.topLocal.default: Top 3 of each profile by state, city and neighbourhood, by rating points (team matches count 3x). Only places with 3+ participants and people with 3+ votes count.
mural.rule.media.video.default: Shows the most viewed highlights video in the app. Needs at least 3 views.
mural.rule.media.radio.default: Shows the most played radio commentary or interview in the app. Needs at least 3 views.
mural.rule.media.journal.default: Shows the most read newspaper report or interview in the app. Needs at least 3 views.
mural.rule.torcida.default: Each fan check-in is worth 10 points, plus 2 if in person. Shows the 10 with the most points. Ties: more check-ins wins.
